qualification: local A05.4 inline-TLB read-fault recovery acceptance; not write/atomic recovery, hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.acceptedBoundary: A generated inline-TLB read resolver records x30 after the architectural walker returns a page fault. The dispatcher resolves that PC through the instruction side table and publishes only the completed prefix.
candidate.rejectedBoundary: Publishing the same prefix for generated inline-TLB write and atomic resolver page faults is unsafe. Those paths retain whole-block rollback and interpreter replay.
candidate.hostControlBoundary: Generated memory epilogues restore incoming FP/LR from append-only context words rather than generated stack storage.

verification.focused: 21 tests in the ABI, metadata-fault, and restartability suites passed.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,548 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the same pinned inputs were executed explicitly.
verification.writeAtomicFailClosed: A real MAP_JIT regression proves inline-TLB write and locked compare-exchange page faults publish neither a host PC nor a speculative context image.

rejectedBroadRun.failure: The init process executed from an invalid user address, raised an NX page fault, panicked the guest, and reset at the same historical boundary as the earlier broad inline-TLB recovery attempt.

disposition.reason: Two independent read-only runs crossed the deterministic broad-candidate reset boundary, four aggregate code-cache wraps, all seven authenticated workloads, and clean ACPI poweroff.
disposition.remainingA05_4Work: Inline write and atomic page faults need an instruction-entry architectural checkpoint or another production-proven mechanism before precise-prefix publication can replace whole-block replay.

limitations: Two passing local runs are a bounded reliability check, not cross-host qualification.
The experiment isolates write/atomic publication as a class but does not identify the exact instruction shape that corrupted init state.
This evidence does not satisfy the greater-than-95-percent dispatcher gate or G1-G5.
